prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which bifunctional small molecules recruit an E3 ubiquitin ligase to a chosen protein so that the cell destroys it, from the first PROTAC to structure-guided design of ternary complexes

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a programmable chemical reaction: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex and the target is removed instead of inhibited. The concept has been reproduced across many laboratories and target classes, it gave biologists a general tool as well as a drug modality, and the cooperativity of the ternary complex gives quantitative design rules that can be measured and tested. Crews and Deshaies established the concept and first proof of principle, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex analysis made it rational chemistry rather than luck. After reading the full first round I keep B011 as my first choice, and no other shortlisted candidate combines this breadth of independent confirmation with demonstrated consequences for what chemists now do.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet a broadly approved drug, and I cannot verify trial outcomes, so the committee could reasonably judge the prize a few years early; the citation should therefore stay on the chemical principle and claim no therapeutic success. A three-person cap also omits Sakamoto and Kim from the founding paper and the whole molecular-glue strand of Handa, Ito and Gray, which is a distinct lineage with its own claim, and that omission must be defended openly. Nitrogenase (B008) has decades of independent confirmation, but its catalytic mechanism is still debated.

responses.point: Heiner disagrees with putting Handa in the trio: the cereblon discovery is a separate discovery about the target of thalidomide, while the PROTAC concept and Ciulli's design rules are what made degradation a general chemical capability, and he would keep Handa and Ito for a later recognition.
responses.response: I have changed my configuration: I now propose Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli in place of Handa. Your argument is the stronger one on what the prize is for. The cereblon work explained a drug retrospectively, whereas the PROTAC line gave a design principle with measurable ternary-complex cooperativity, and a citation about a general chemical capability should name the people who built that capability. I still regard cereblon as the best-measured mechanism in the field, and I would rather say openly that the glue strand is left for a later prize than blur the citation to cover it.

responses.point: Johan holds that the glue strand arose from serendipity and retrospective explanation, whereas the PROTAC strand is a rational design principle and closer to a game-changer, and he wants the citation kept to the degradation principle with E3 recruitment and no claim of therapeutic success.
responses.response: I accept both points. The citation I now propose is worded around recruitment of an E3 ligase and the ternary-complex design rules, and it makes no clinical claim. On timing we agree that the record is long, with twenty years since the first PROTAC and wide independent reproduction, but I would stress that reproduction of the mechanism is what the criterion needs here, and that is in hand. Whether an approved drug appears before the announcement changes how the prize looks, not whether the chemistry is correct, and I would hold my first place either way.

responses.point: Peter ranks B058 first as a mature, independently confirmed physical framework for protein electron transfer and ranks B011 fourth on clinical immaturity, while himself flagging priority overlap with Marcus, Dutton and Moser, and Hopfield.
responses.response: I have heard the maturity argument and I do not dismiss it, but it is not the main issue for me. For B058 the question the chair raised stands: what did Gray and Winkler discover that Marcus theory, Hopfield, and Dutton and Moser had not already established? Until a citation can be drawn narrowly enough to answer that, I rank it behind B011 on novelty of consequence. I would ask Peter whether, if B058 cannot reach five votes, he could accept B011 with the narrowly worded PROTAC citation, since his own stated reservation is clinical validation and not the mechanism.

responses.point: Peter ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B055) first for daily use and clean two-person credit, and asks whether the degrader chemistry is chemically innovative; he accepts that the concept came from cell biology and that the medicinal chemistry rules are the chemical achievement.
responses.response: On chemical innovation I think the answer is yes in the sense you describe: heterobifunctional design with linker optimisation, and cooperativity in a ternary complex, are chemistry decisions that determine whether degradation occurs. I do not question the adoption or the clean credit for B055, and I accept that it needed a different mechanistic solution from the 2010 C-C couplings. My remaining difference is one of weight, between ubiquity of a method and a new capability, and I would not call it a difference in scientific rigour. If B011 does reach a majority I would ask you to consider whether the narrow PROTAC citation addresses your concern.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts that the molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) is omitted from this prize and left for later, and whether Sakamoto and Kim can be defended as omitted.
Whether clinical validation of degraders will be sufficient by the announcement, which I cannot verify.
Whether the nitrogenase mechanism (B008) is settled enough to rank above degraders, given that N2 binding and the E4 state remain debated.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile; none of the shortlisted candidates is in my own nucleotide-metabolism research area or my Umeå, Cold Spring Harbor or Wallenberg collaborations.
